target_customer: Robotics hobbyists, researchers and developers buying low cost open source humanoid robots (K-Bot, earlier Stompy)
problem: Humanoid robots were expensive and closed. K-Scale aimed to sell an open source, 3D printable humanoid at a consumer or researcher price.
business_model: Hardware sales and pre-orders of open source humanoid robots
product_category: Consumer and research humanoid robotics, open source hardware

founders.name: Benjamin Bolte
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Matthew Freed
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as 'MechE + AI'. Prior employers not listed.

exit.reason: CEO said he overestimated how easily the company could raise a Series A and had bet on the costly K-Bot launch; IP was released under open licenses.

competitors.name: Figure AI
competitors.what: Venture backed general purpose humanoid robot company
competitors.traction_then: Raised a $675M round announced 2024-02-29 with a reported $2.6B valuation and an OpenAI collaboration

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing a bipedal humanoid with walking, manipulation and a sub $10K bill of materials, plus later a production robot, needs mechanical, electronics and controls work that is hard for a team of about 10.

defensibility.rationale: The designs were open sourced on purpose and shut down released all IP, so copying was easy; the intended moat was community and cost, which was not shown to hold.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded humanoid makers pursued industrial use cases; no source shows they acquired or copied K-Scale. Unitree sold its H1 at under $90,000 in 2024.

market_need_then: Interest in humanoid robots surged in 2023 and 2024 with Tesla Optimus and Figure, while low cost open platforms for researchers were scarce. Pre-orders reportedly exceeded $2 million by one account (Failory), which is unverified.

branding.name_origin: One wiki says it references the Kardashev Scale, but no primary company source confirms this.
branding.domain_note: Used kscale.dev rather than an exact .com; the site did not resolve in a later check.

identity.mascot_or_character: Stompy, a 4 foot humanoid prototype whose name was reportedly chosen by vote (one source, may refer to a different project)
identity.voice_and_tone: Open and hacker style, CEO publicly wrote a candid farewell letter

branding.brand_signature: Open source humanoid robots for everyone, with the Stompy prototype
branding.community_and_virality: Press and AI Engineer conference talk coverage of Stompy and the K-Bot; no merch found

brand_strength.rationale: Got notable YC and trade press coverage and a clear open source positioning, but little evidence the brand itself drove sales; the company folded.

pivots.to: Higher priced K-Bot production humanoid (roughly $9K to $15K by different reports)
pivots.why: Bolte said he bet the company on the K-Bot launch instead of the cheaper Z-Bot.

outcome_analysis: K-Scale got into YC in Winter 2024 and gained attention for open source humanoids, but the K-Bot was costly to build at scale. By the CEO's own account a Series A of about $20 million was expected after 100 pre-orders, investors were skeptical, and the company wound down in November 2025 with reportedly about $400K left. The open source IP was released on shutdown.
notes: Funding conflicts: CB Insights says $4.75M total over 7 rounds and a $50M valuation in Feb 2025 (single database, unverified); StartupHub says $10M; Failory style post mortem says $5.0M. The $500K pre seed rests on Preqin and VCBacked. Only two of the 7 CB Insights rounds are recorded because the rest are not itemized in sources I could open. The Feb 2025 round amount is unknown; the stage label is 'other' because no source states it (one source says a $4M seed). Founding year 2024 per YC; other sources say 2023. Kscale.dev did not resolve during the check.
